newsitem.title: USA: U.S. should reduce tariffs for Caribbean--senators.
newsitem.headline: U.S. should reduce tariffs for Caribbean--senators.

text.p: The United States should reduce tariffs on imports from Caribbean countries in order to offset unfair competition from NAFTA nations, particularly Mexico, two senators said on Thursday.

"The North American Free Trade Agreement has ... unfairly impacted the CBI (Caribbean Basin Initiative) countries and companies invested in them," Arizona Republican John McCain and Florida Democrat Bob Graham said in a letter to the Senate Finance Committee.
Because of NAFTA, goods imported from Mexico are becoming less expensive than comparable products from the Caribbean, because tariffs on goods from Caribbean nations are higher, the senators said.
NAFTA has also diverted investment in manufacturing operations away from the Caribbean and toward Mexico, according to the senators.
"Companies in the Caribbean Basin are considering relocating to Mexico because of the less-costly trade restrictions," their letter said.
About 275,000 American jobs depend on Caribbean trade, it said.
High tariffs, coupled with the World Trade Organization's (WTO) recent banana ruling, might encourage more illicit trade and drug trafficking, it said.
In May the WTO struck down a preferential banana export agreement between the European Union and the countries of the Caribbean.
The House of Representatives included the tariff reduction proposal in its budget reconciliation bill, but the Senate had not addressed the matter, McCain and Graham said.
